proof:
# Exact obstruction to a stronger parity-budget lemma

The plausible inequality

max_{y in P intersect Z^n} (unnormalized halfspace depth of y)
>= max_{r in (Z/2Z)^n} |P intersect (r+2Z^n)|

is false. This is not a counterexample to the requested theorem.

Let P=conv{(-3,-1),(3,3),(1,3),(-1,2)}. Equivalently,

P={ (x,y): 3y-2x>=3, y<=3, 2y-x<=5, 2y-3x<=7 }.

Enumerating integer x between -3 and 3 in these inequalities gives exactly

S={(-3,-1),(-2,0),(-1,1),(-1,2),(0,1),(0,2),(1,2),(1,3),(2,3),(3,3)}.

The odd/odd parity class contains four points: (-3,-1),(-1,1),(1,3),(3,3). Nevertheless every point of S lies in a closed halfspace containing at most three points of S, as the following exact certificate shows. Each cut is given by a*x+b*y>=c.

| Point | (a,b,c) | Points in cut |
|---|---|---|
| (-3,-1) | (-1,0,3) | (-3,-1) |
| (-2,0) | (-1,0,2) | (-3,-1),(-2,0) |
| (-1,1) | (-1,-1,0) | (-3,-1),(-2,0),(-1,1) |
| (-1,2) | (-1,1,3) | (-1,2) |
| (0,1) | (3,-4,-4) | (0,1),(3,3) |
| (0,2) | (-2,3,6) | (-1,2),(0,2),(1,3) |
| (1,2) | (2,-1,0) | (1,2),(2,3),(3,3) |
| (1,3) | (-1,3,8) | (1,3) |
| (2,3) | (1,0,2) | (2,3),(3,3) |
| (3,3) | (1,0,3) | (3,3) |

Every row is verified by direct substitution into its integer linear inequality. Thus the maximal unnormalized depth is at most three, strictly below the largest parity-class cardinality four. The requested n=2,d=0 lower bound is 10/4=2.5, so the example does not challenge it.
